question: Among samans, meters, months, and seasons, which forms does the Lord identify as himself?
premises: bṛhatsāma is the great saman among samans
gāyatrī is the meter among meters
mārgaśīrṣa is the month among months
kusumākara is the flower-maker among seasons
the speaker identifies each as himself
inference: The Lord declares himself as the foremost representative in each listed category.
uncertainties: kusumākaraḥ is rendered as flower-maker and may refer to spring
the fused forms mārgaśīrṣo'ham and chandasāmaham are parsed according to the supplied glosses
plain_english: Among the samans I am the Brihat-saman; among meters I am Gayatri; among months I am Margashirsha; among seasons I am the flower-maker.
